messages:
Alice H: Heads up — onboarding for model `primeflow-3b` incoming. Weights + tokenizer uploaded to s3://redwood-inbound/primeflow-3b/ . Need ops to confirm checksums, KMS wrapping, and registry gating. cc @Dana S @Ben M

Dana S: On it. Expected manifest: sha256 per-file, size in bytes, signer cert fingerprint, and a provenance.json with source_tag + ingest_ticket. I'll run a quick sha check now.

Ben M: Do we also want to persist quantized variants separately (e.g., float32, 8bit, 4bit)? My recommendation: store canonical fp32 + separate quantized artifacts with clear tags in the registry so rollbacks are easy. Add "format" and "quant_profile" fields to provenance.json.

Carlos R: I'll queue smoke tests for tokenization and basic generation once checksums pass. Need a small prompt set — @Alice H can you attach 10 short prompts? Also watch out for tokenizer mismatches; include `vocab_hash` in the manifest. Example checksum command I ran locally:```bash
sha256sum weights.bin > weights.bin.sha256
sha256sum tokenizer.json > tokenizer.json.sha256
```

ingest-bot: registry ticket RG-3241 created for primeflow-3b ingest. Current status: awaiting_checksums -> assigned to Dana S. ETA 2h.

Emily L: I'll produce detached signatures with the model-signing key `models-prod`. Output will be weights.bin.sig and tokenizer.json.sig; uploading to s3 path + adding `signer_fingerprint` to provenance.json. For KMS wrap, we should encrypt the symmetric key with KMS and store `kms_key_id` in the manifest.

Alice H: Perfect. Proposed minimal provenance.json (edit as needed):```json
{
  "model_name": "primeflow-3b",
  "version": "2026-03-20-01",
  "source": "partner-x/consignment-789",
  "files": [
    {"name": "weights.bin", "sha256": "<sha256>", "size": "<bytes>", "format": "pytorch"},
    {"name": "tokenizer.json", "sha256": "<sha256>", "size": "<bytes>", "vocab_hash": "<hash>"}
  ],
  "signer_fingerprint": "<fingerprint>",
  "kms_key_id": "projects/redwood/keys/models-prod",
  "quant_profiles": ["fp32","int8"],
  "ingest_ticket": "RG-3241"
}
```

Dana S: Running checksums now. If everything matches I'll mark RG-3241 -> checks_passed and kick the ingest pipeline which will: verify sigs -> create registry entry -> trigger smoke tests.

Ben M: One ask for the smoke job: record per-prompt tokenization diffs + perplexity on small eval set. If quant experiments deviate >2% on quality metric we gate automatic rollout.

Carlos R: Noted. I'll attach the prompt set in the ticket and post initial smoke results in this thread.

Alice H: Timeline: aim to complete these steps EOD today. If ops hits any mismatch, escalate to @Emily L for re-sign and to legal for provenance questions. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Emily L: Got it, standing by for checksum pass to sign.

Dana S: checksums: weights.bin sha256 OK, tokenizer.json mismatch (vocab_hash different). Marking RG-3241 -> needs_vendor_fix.

Alice H: Thanks — looping in partner contact. We'll hold ingest until vendor provides corrected tokenizer or a mapping table.

Carlos R: I'll still run tokenization compatibility tests against both tokenizers to quantify diffs once vendor provides mapping.

Alice H: Update in ticket once vendor responds.
